title: Asset and Drop Again
premise: Odile Villalobos, a former intelligence asset turned interpreter for a faltering peace delegation, discovers the safe house she was once trained in has been listed online with interior photos — proof someone is burning the network's secrets, and her cover with them. As the delegation collapses and her handler's loyalties fracture, Odile realizes the listing is bait set by the man who trained her, forcing her to choose between destroying the network or protecting the delegation member she has come to love. She burns the network from within, trading her old identity for a chance at an ordinary life, though the final photo in the listing suggests someone is still watching.
about_author: Edmund Ashgrove is the pen name of a former NGO logistics coordinator who spent a decade in contested border regions before turning to fiction. He writes thrillers about the people who translate wars — literally and figuratively — for a living.

chapters.title: The Listing
chapters.summary: Odile, interpreting a tense ceasefire briefing, idly browses real estate sites and finds the safe house where she was trained years ago — every room photographed, including the wall where her codename was once written. Her hands shake through the translation. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: dread masquerading as nostalgia; the past has a public address now.

chapters.title: Go-Bag Rules
chapters.summary: Odile checks her packed bag, rehearses her cover story, and maps the delegation's vulnerabilities for her handler, Marek — while noticing he asks one question too many about the listing. A quiet dinner with delegate Tomás Reyes reveals her growing attachment to the man she may be betraying. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: the ache of living two lives, and the first crack in her professionalism.

chapters.title: Open House
chapters.summary: Odile visits the listed house under a false name and finds the training wall repainted but the safe behind it intact — and freshly emptied. Someone got there first. A neighbor mentions a woman with a delegation lanyard. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: paranoia sharpening into purpose; the hunt has begun, and she may already be prey.

chapters.title: The Delegation Frays
chapters.summary: Ceasefire talks collapse over a staged border incident; Odile translates accusations she knows are scripted by the very network she served. Marek orders her to plant a listening device in Tomás's suite. She does — then lies about where she placed it. POV: Odile, with a brief Marek interlude. Emotional beat: complicity curdling; duty and love pull in opposite directions.

chapters.title: What the Wall Remembered
chapters.summary: Odile decodes the listing's photo sequence as a message in her old training cipher: coordinates, a date, and the word RECRUIT. The trainer she believed dead, Ilse Brandt, is alive and rebuilding. Marek's questions reveal he may be reporting to Brandt too. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: cold clarity; the network never let her go, it was only waiting.

chapters.title: Tomás
chapters.summary: Tomás confronts Odile about the device — he found it, and he knows she placed it. Instead of exposing her, he asks why. She tells him a partial truth: the network trained her, the delegation was chosen to fail, and he is collateral. They become reluctant allies, and something more. POV: Tomás. Emotional beat: intimacy forged under threat; trust as an act of defiance.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: Marek discovers Odile's deception and gives her an ultimatum: deliver Tomás to Brandt's people at the resumption talks or be exposed as a former asset to both delegations. Odile photographs Marek's own double-dealings as insurance. POV: Odile, with a Marek interlude. Emotional beat: cornered resolve; survival now requires betrayal — the only question is of whom.

chapters.title: The Second Safe House
chapters.summary: Odile and Tomás follow the cipher's coordinates to a farmhouse where Brandt is holding the delegation's leaked negotiation dossier. Odile walks in alone, playing the recruit Brandt always wanted, while Tomás waits with a borrowed radio and her contingency plan. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: terror disciplined into performance; the student returning to the teacher's table.

chapters.title: Asset and Drop
chapters.summary: Brandt offers Odile her old life back; Marek arrives to collect Tomás and finds Odile already wearing a wire, broadcasting Brandt's confession to both delegations and two intelligence services. Marek turns his gun on Odile; Tomás's distraction lets her drop him — her handler, her trainer's instrument — for good. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: the climax of choice; she burns the network with her own voice.

chapters.title: For Sale, Furnished
chapters.summary: Weeks later, the peace process limps forward on the wreckage of the scandal, and Odile — officially dead, unofficially relocated — unpacks a go-bag she finally empties. Tomás arrives with keys to a small apartment. On a real estate site, a new listing appears: her old safe house, sold, with one new photo — a figure in the doorway, watching. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: hard-won belonging shadowed by the price of survival; the watcher is never named.
